mia (devex): Heads up — saw two customer reports where the async python client blows up on non-JSON error bodies. 502 returned text/html and aiohttp raised ContentTypeError inside our client.

devon (py-sdk): Can you paste a short repro + stack so I can see where we call resp.json()?

mia (devex): Sure — here's the traceback from their app logs: 
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/main.py", line 42, in handle
    resp_json = await client.post("/infer", json=payload)
  File "/venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/aiohttp/client.py", line 1072, in json
    raise ContentTypeError(request_info, history, message=msg)
aiohttp.ContentTypeError: 0, message='Attempt to decode JSON with unexpected mimetype: text/html'
```

alex r: We currently call `await resp.json()` without a fallback. If the server returns text/html or text/plain we just bubble the decode error up and we lose raw body.

samir (backend): Also our exception model is inconsistent. `HttpError` has `.status` in some places, `.status_code` in others, and no `raw_body` or `content_type` field. `request_id` sometimes comes from headers, sometimes from `meta` in parsed JSON.

mia (devex): Repro snippet (async):
```py
async def call():
    async with client.session.post(url, json=payload) as r:
        data = await r.json()  # raises ContentTypeError for text/html
        client._raise_for_status(r, data)
```

devon (py-sdk): Proposal: on JSON decode failures we should capture `raw_text = await resp.text()` and attach it to an enriched `HttpError` instance as `raw_text` or `raw_body`. Also add `parsed_json` which is None when decode fails. Keep `status_code`, `headers`, `request_id` as first-class fields. Set `__cause__` to the original decode error so folks can inspect it.

alex r: That sounds reasonable. For compatibility, add property aliases `.body` -> `.raw_text` and `.status` -> `.status_code`. Document the new fields in changelog.

samir (backend): Retry behavior: we treat 5xx as non-retriable if raise_for_status raises immediately? I think decode failures during 5xx should be considered transient (maybe server returned HTML). We should let the retryer handle decode errors for 5xx by default.

devon (py-sdk): Agreed. Plan for PR:
1) Catch ContentTypeError / JSONDecodeError when calling `resp.json()` inside the client.
2) Attempt `raw_text = await resp.text()` and include in exception.
3) Extend `HttpError` dataclass to include `status_code`, `headers`, `raw_text`, `parsed_json`, `request_id`. Keep old properties as aliases.
4) Mark decode failures as retryable when status_code >= 500 (configurable).
5) Add unit tests that simulate `content-type: text/plain` and `text/html`.

mia (devex): Test assertion idea: `exc.raw_text == 'Service overloaded'` and `exc.parsed_json is None`. Also test that `exc.__cause__` is instance of `ContentTypeError` or `JSONDecodeError`.

alex r: +1. Also add typing stubs so `HttpError` is properly typed in py. We should run mypy in CI for the sdk package after this.

sre-bot: deploybot: canary build for py-sdk/ci #456 passed :white_check_mark:

devon (py-sdk): I'll open the PR and link here. Plan to keep the public surface stable by adding aliases and deprecate the old names in the next major.

mia (devex): Thanks — I can repro with a small Flask app if you want a live test. Ping me once PR is up and I'll verify with the customer's example. :thumbsup:

devon (py-sdk): TY — putting together the branch now.

alex r: Minor nit: add a short example in the README showing how to inspect `exc.raw_text` and `exc.parsed_json` for debugging.

samir (backend): Also note: some internal services return 200 + `{'error': ...}`. We should consider a hook that lets callers translate success payloads into errors based on content. Not part of this PR but filing an issue.

mia (devex): Filed issue #382 for content-based error predicates.

devon (py-sdk): PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/py-sdk/pull/789 — includes tests and typing updates.

mia (devex): Confirmed repro works with PR branch — raw_text preserved and retry behavior fixed in local test. Thanks everyone.
